Born: October 25, 1984, 7:58 AM local time, Santa Barbara, California, USA. Source: Astro-Databank, Rodden rating AA.

The AA rating means the birth time comes from a birth certificate or an equally solid record, so the rising sign, the Midheaven and the houses below can be read at face value. Open Katy Perry's chart on Astrolas to follow along.

One sign owns this chart. The Sun, Moon, Mercury, Saturn and Pluto all sit in Scorpio, and the Ascendant lands in Scorpio too, at 10°47'. That is six points out of a possible fourteen, packed into the same narrow stretch of sky.

She was born Katheryn Hudson, the daughter of two pentecostal pastors, and recorded gospel music under her own name before she became Katy Perry. A sign built around control, privacy and reinvention, running six placements deep, is a fitting engine for that switch.

muc.ten: Five planets in Scorpio, plus the rising sign
doan: In order of degree: Pluto at 2°05', the Sun at 2°23', the Ascendant at 10°47', Mercury at 11°59', Saturn at 17°05' and the Moon at 17°57'. All Scorpio.

The library's Sun in Scorpio reads as intensity and magnetism, guided by Pluto, with a deep hunger for life and love and the discipline to confront what others look away from. Its shadow is possessiveness and a pull toward shutting down when hurt, though the library compares the sign's resilience to a phoenix: setbacks get absorbed, then turned into transformation. The Moon in Scorpio keeps real feeling behind a calm, controlled surface, suspicious of motives until trust is earned. Mercury in Scorpio wants the truth under the small talk and keeps its own counsel until it has something worth saying. Saturn in Scorpio sharpens all of it into ambition and a capacity to rebuild after a real crisis.

The Sun and Pluto sit together in the 12th house, the library's house of privacy and the inner world. The Ascendant, Mercury, Saturn and the Moon cluster in the 1st, the house of the self other people meet first.

muc.ten: Sun conjunct Pluto in the 12th house
doan: The tightest aspect in the chart sits here: the Sun at 2°23' Scorpio and Pluto at 2°05' Scorpio, a conjunction with an orb of 0°17', both in the 12th house.

The library reads Sun conjunct Pluto as extreme energy and an iron will, with the kind of psychological insight that lets someone read a room without being told anything, and a caution against letting that power turn into a need to control or dominate. Its note on the Sun in the 12th house describes someone who can be shy or short on confidence early on, who performs best from behind the scenes, and who usually finds that this changes at some point before the age of thirty, once an inner reserve of strength has been built.

Her own timeline fits. She was still working in gospel music under her birth name in the early 2000s. "I Kissed a Girl" did not reach number one until 2008, when she was twenty-three. Teenage Dream, the 2010 album that made her inescapable, arrived when she was twenty-five and went on to produce five number-one singles on the Billboard Hot 100, tying a record Michael Jackson set with Bad.

muc.ten: Moon conjunct Saturn in Scorpio, in the 1st house
doan: The Moon at 17°57' and Saturn at 17°05' Scorpio are conjunct, orb 0°52', and both sit in the 1st house.

The library ties this pairing to the past, specifically a family environment heavy on rules and discipline, which can breed self-doubt and a cool, distant exterior. Its remedy is self-control paired with safe, supportive relationships that slowly rebuild confidence. In the 1st house, both placements show up immediately: the Moon here reads a room through a strong sixth sense, while Saturn here can look reserved or hard to approach, mostly because it is quietly watching before it opens up to anyone.

Her parents, Keith and Mary Hudson, are both pentecostal pastors, and she grew up on gospel music inside a household built on church rules. The library's language, discipline learned early, a controlled surface built over something far more intense, matches a performer who spent her twenties building one of pop's most colorful, exaggerated public faces.

muc.ten: Mercury conjunct the Ascendant in Scorpio
doan: Mercury at 11°59' Scorpio sits close to the Ascendant at 10°47' Scorpio, a conjunction with an orb of 1°13'.

The library's Mercury in Scorpio wants to dig past the surface of any subject and speaks only when there is something worth saying. In the 1st house, it spends real time in quiet self-reflection, weighing a thought before it is said out loud. The aspect itself, Mercury conjunct the Ascendant, the library reads as a gift for talking, thinking and writing, guided by nonstop curiosity, with the caution that all that mental motion can scatter focus and strain the mind.

She writes or co-writes the bulk of her own catalog, and that same quick, pointed instinct shows up in her public voice: a run of quotable one-liners in interviews, and several seasons as a judge on American Idol, a job that runs entirely on fast commentary.

muc.ten: Venus in Sagittarius, also rising in the 1st house
doan: Venus sits at 6°33' Sagittarius, in the 1st house, among the Scorpio cluster at the Ascendant even though the sign itself is different.

The library's Venus in Sagittarius loves with an adventurous, enthusiastic spirit and needs real personal freedom inside any relationship. It notes that people with this placement often marry late or choose to stay single, since independence tends to outrank a formal tie. In the 1st house, the library adds a graceful appearance and a natural gift for diplomacy, with a love of art and beauty and a downside of complacency.

She married Russell Brand in 2010; they divorced in 2012. She later had a long engagement to Orlando Bloom, with whom she has a daughter, Daisy Dove, born in 2020, without rushing into marriage, a pattern the library's text names directly.

muc.ten: Uranus and Neptune in Sagittarius, in the money house
doan: Uranus at 11°25' and Neptune at 29°13' Sagittarius both sit in the 2nd house, alongside Jupiter.

Uranus and Neptune here are generational, shared by anyone born in the same years: Uranus for a pioneering streak against rigid structures, Neptune for an idealism that seeks truth through religion, philosophy or a wider cause. The library makes both personal through the 2nd house: Uranus brings erratic, unpredictable money, sudden gains as easily as sudden losses, built on a genuinely unconventional set of values; Neptune brings strong financial intuition paired with real impracticality and a deep attachment to sentimental objects over cash itself.

The thread traces back to the same childhood: a gospel upbringing built on religious conviction, landing here in the house of resources rather than belief alone. Her career since has leaned into visually extravagant, costly stage concepts and into ventures beyond music, including a footwear line, the kind of financial swings the library's texts describe.
Mars sits at 14°25' Capricorn in the 3rd house. Jupiter sits at 7°49' Capricorn in the 2nd.

The library's Mars in Capricorn holds its energy in check until it is truly needed, backed by real endurance and willpower, driving a career built on ambition, status and financial security that gets worked for practically rather than chased all at once. Jupiter in Capricorn runs the same way: success built step by step through discipline rather than handed over by luck, paired with a talent for business and a habit of saving carefully until the moment is right to spend. In the 3rd house, the library's Mars adds an outspoken, quick-reacting streak, always ready to defend a position in an argument. In the 2nd house, Jupiter adds a good read on profitable opportunities other people miss, as long as overspending stays in check.

That mix of discipline and well-timed risk runs through her business side: a footwear and fragrance line alongside the music, and world tours built methodically from one album cycle to the next. Two more razor-tight contacts touch the Midheaven, Saturn square MC at an orb of 0°34' and the Moon square MC at 1°26', but the library has no entries for either aspect, or for the Leo Midheaven itself, so this piece leaves them as chart facts only.

muc.ten: What the chart adds up to
doan: The chart doesn't explain a hit song, and it can't account for stagecraft. What it shows is where the weight sits: six points in Scorpio split between a private 12th house and an exposed 1st house, with the Sun and Pluto locked together at the center of it. Mercury glued to the Ascendant gives the fast, quotable public voice, Venus, Uranus and Neptune in Sagittarius carry the old religious thread into risk and reinvention, and Capricorn's Mars and Jupiter supply the patience that turned it into an actual career.
Open Katy Perry's chart on Astrolas, find the Scorpio cluster around the Ascendant, then compare it with a chart you know.
Scorpio, at 10°47', based on her AA-rated birth time of 7:58 AM. Mercury sits almost exactly on it, a conjunction with an orb of 1°13'.
Both in Scorpio. Her Sun is at 2°23' in the 12th house, conjunct Pluto. Her Moon is at 17°57' in the 1st house, conjunct Saturn.

Six placements in Scorpio: the Sun, Moon, Mercury, Saturn and Pluto, plus the Ascendant itself. Add the tight Sun-Pluto conjunction at the center of it and the chart's center of gravity is hard to miss.
